analysis.title: PAIN Bitcoin has lost over $10,000 in a week
key_insights: Bitcoin is down roughly 25% since October 21. The latest weekend sell-off triggered nearly $2 billion in crypto liquidations.
Selling accelerated after BTC broke below its 200-day moving average, around $73,000.
Spot BTC ETFs lost $2.35 billion over the last two weeks (The Block) and have seen seven straight days of outflows. The note reads this as deteriorating institutional demand.

MARA sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1 billion in six weeks, equal to 40% of its September-end holdings. It used $750 million to repay Bitcoin-backed loans and has sold more than 40,000 BTC in 2026. Future sales could help fund its AI data-center plans.
Bitcoin is again trading below Strategy's average purchase price. The note says the open question is whether Strategy can keep buying while others sell, not whether it will be forced to liquidate.

The note floats a theory that investors are selling liquid assets, including Bitcoin, to raise cash for Anthropic IPO allocations. Per figures attributed to Strive's Matt Cole, Bitcoin fell 19% in the 50 days before the SpaceX IPO and about 18% over the comparable period before Anthropic. The note calls the link possibly a coincidence.
Perpetual funding rates turned negative on Binance, OKX and Bybit on November 13. Traders are now paying to hold shorts, not only being liquidated on longs.
Volume spiked sharply during the weekend liquidation.

NVDA has traded lower for 6 consecutive weeks, its longest losing streak since 2012. China's stock market was lower in 13 of the last 14 weeks, its weakest such stretch on record. The note ties both to Bitcoin's decline.
crypto_views: Bitcoin is down roughly a quarter since October 21, with nearly $2 billion of liquidations in the latest weekend flush.
Spot BTC ETF outflows total $2.35 billion over two weeks and seven straight days. The ETF bid has turned into an ETF offer.
MARA, a large miner, has sold 13,597 BTC in six weeks (40% of its September-end holdings) and more than 40,000 BTC in 2026, partly to repay loans and partly to fund AI data-center ambitions.
Bitcoin is trading below Strategy's average purchase price. Whether Strategy keeps buying is the key question.
Possible rotation theory: investors selling Bitcoin to fund Anthropic IPO allocations, compared with Bitcoin's 19% drop before the SpaceX IPO.
risk_factors: Further spot ETF outflows after seven straight days of selling.
Strategy may be unable to keep buying with Bitcoin below its average purchase price.
More miner selling, as MARA has sold 40% of its September-end holdings.
Capital rotation into AI IPOs (Anthropic) draining demand for liquid assets.
Negative funding shows shorts are increasingly crowded in.
charts_described: Chart from secretsatoshis.com shows BTC breaking below its 200-day moving average around $73,000, after which selling accelerated.
Farside chart shows seven straight days of spot BTC ETF outflows, with $2.35 billion leaving over two weeks.
CoinGlass derivatives data shows funding turning negative on Binance, OKX and Bybit on November 13.
vol_and_positioning: Funding rates turned negative on Binance, OKX and Bybit on November 13, which means traders are paying to be short.
Weekend liquidations came with a serious volume spike, and nearly $2 billion of crypto positions were liquidated.
The note says leverage is being flushed out and buyers have seemingly disappeared.
